title: la.bitmaker.usage.recorded v1
description: One metered usage fact, as a CloudEvent (structured mode). ADR 0013: this schema is the contract between the Products and billing, and it is open: a new Product, metric or dimension needs no change here. What billing meters and prices is its catalogue, not this schema. Product-specific rules live in each Product's profile (profiles/). The four time rules in ADR 0013 go with it. Money is never in an event: prices live in OpenMeter's rate cards.

source.description: The producing Product, a lowercase slug fixed for its lifetime (estela, bitmaker-proxy, ...). Half of OpenMeter's dedupe identity (source, id): changing it re-bills every retry. data.reporter carries the same value.

id.description: The fact's idempotency key, deterministic across retries: {source}:{scope}:{...}:v{n}, e.g. estela:job:{jid}:slice:{slice_index}:v1. It starts with its own source (a Product's profile enforces that). Never a random id.

subject.description: The paying Org's billing account id, stored on the Project or Proxy endpoint when it was created (ADR 0004, ADR 0005). Never a User.

time.description: UTC, with a Z. A slice: its interval_start, on the 5-minute grid. An adjustment: when it is sent. Never ahead of the producer's clock (ADR 0013, rule 1).

allOf.description: A slice is stamped at its interval_start, on the UTC 5-minute grid, so it never straddles a period boundary (periods start at 00:00 UTC, ADR 0011).

reporter.description: The same value as the event's source: the one copy a meter can read (envelope attributes are not addressable).

kind.description: Only these reach OpenMeter. A Product's own job totals (JOB_CLOSE) stay in the Product as its reconciliation anchor (ADR 0013).

resource_kind.description: What the usage ran in, as a lowercase name (spider_job, project_storage, proxy_endpoint, ...). The Product names its own.

resource_id.description: Which one, for drill-down through the event list; never a meter dimension (unbounded).

dimensions.description: Everything a meter may group by or a price may depend on (project_id, machine_tier, proxy_class, ...): bounded, short string values. Meters read them as $.dimensions.<key> (research §31). A price that depends on a dimension always has a catch-all line, so a missing or unknown value is billed, not lost (ADR 0013).

references_id.description: An ADJUSTMENT: the id of the fact it corrects, or of the slice it replaces when that slice was late (ADR 0013, rule 2).

metrics.description: Integers in base units, the unit in the name: *_seconds, *_bytes, *_count, *_byte_seconds (storage: bytes held x seconds held). Open: a new metric needs no schema change, only a meter on billing's side to be counted. Invoices convert (GiB = 2^30 bytes, GiB-hours, hours), so events never round.

allOf.description: A slice carries no negative value.
An adjustment says what it corrects and why.
